content_units: Game Night Flow for 19:00-23:00

A strong lineup here should start with ultra-fast teach games, build into team energy, give the competitive player a satisfying strategic slot, and end with something social and light. This order minimizes rules fatigue for the newer players and avoids front-loading the evening with the heaviest explanation.
Recommended Lineup and Time Blocks
Time   Game   Players   Estimated Play   Why it fits this spot
19:00-19:20     Just One     6   20 min   Best opener: almost no rules overhead, cooperative, funny, and immediately welcoming for new players.
19:20-19:45     Wavelength     6   25 min   Keeps the group talking and laughing while still being easy to learn; ideal once everyone is warmed up.
19:45-20:25     Codenames     6   40 min   First “main event” team game; familiar word-association style makes it accessible while adding tension.
20:25-20:35     Break / snacks reset     6   10 min   Good natural pause before moving into more competitive play.
20:35-21:05     Coup     6   30 min   Short, sharp, competitive, and high-energy; gives the very competitive guest a spotlight without dragging.
21:05-21:50     Azul     4-4 or rotate table focus   45 min   This is the most satisfying strategy slot, but teach it after everyone is comfortable. Best as the “serious game” of the night.
21:50-22:20     Sushi Go Party!     6   30 min   Quick drafting game that feels breezy after Azul; easy to explain and keeps all 6 engaged.
22:20-23:00     Decrypto     6   40 min   Strong closer for a now-calibrated group; deeper than the opener games, but by this point everyone will be ready for it.
Why This Order Works for This Group
Option 1:   Just One first     Lowest-friction start, instant participation, no pressure on new players   Best for the guest who hates long rules
Learn Just One
Option 2:   Wavelength before heavier games     Builds table chemistry and confidence through discussion   Best social bridge game
Learn Wavelength
Option 3:   Coup before Azul     Lets the competitive player get a fast, sharp contest without committing the whole group to a long teach   Best tension spike
Learn Coup
Option 4:   Azul as the strategy centerpiece     Gives the evening one richer, more thoughtful game after everyone is settled   Best “main strategy” slot
Learn Azul
Games to Skip or Use as Backups
-   Ticket to Ride  : Great game, but for a 4-hour mixed-experience night it is a bit long for this specific lineup and overlaps with Azul as the “teach-and-think” slot.

-   Codenames vs Decrypto  : Keeping both works because one lands mid-evening as accessible team play and the other closes with more challenge. If the group seems mentally tired, cut   Decrypto   and replay   Wavelength   instead.
-   If Azul only supports 4 in your edition  : Swap   Azul   out for   Ticket to Ride   only if your group is okay with a slightly longer rules teach and a more traditional board-game feel.
Quick Host Notes
- Teach each game in under 3 minutes where possible; explain only enough to start the first round.
- Seat one experienced player beside each newer player for clue/team games.
- Put the competitive guest on a team during   Codenames   or   Decrypto   so intensity helps the group rather than dominating it.
- If energy dips after 21:30, skip   Decrypto   and end with a second round of   Sushi Go Party!   or   Wavelength  .
